newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Bangladesh, on behalf of the least developed countries, urged the major industrialised nations to consider measures, including debt relief, facilitate direct inmvestment and duty free treatment for the LDCs.
The government may allow deposed military ruler, Hussain Mohammad Ershad, to travel abroad for medical purpose early next month.
Rain waters rolling down from across the border may cause flooding in northeastern districts.
Several thousand farmers in northern Thakurgaon district on Saturday put up barricade on the highway, demanding fair price of paddy.
Opposition lawmakers on Saturday criticised the 1997/98 budget, saying the fiscal policies were aimed at protecting trade interests of India.
Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Saturday demanded an inquiry committee, comprising experts from home and abroad, to find out causes of the fire at Magurchhara gas field.
Eleven industrial sub-sectors have been given "thrust sector" status in the fiith five year plan, beginning on July 1.
Industries Minister Tofael Ahmed on Saturday said the sugar mills, if they can show profit, would not be privatised. REUTER
